editorial.headline: Government Residential Care for Mental Disability and Substance Misuse
editorial.standfirst: A government-run residential-care activity whose social purpose is clear—and whose route is closed to foreign ownership nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, this is not an available registration in Bali today. The activity is defined as government-managed residential care for people with mental or intellectual disabilities, as well as people affected by narcotics, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, regardless of age. It is care delivered where people live: supervision, counselling and services form part of the same residential setting.

Its scope is deliberately broad within that setting. It includes treatment facilities for victims of illicit-drug misuse; recovery homes for people with mental or intellectual disabilities and for those affected by drug misuse; group homes; health halfway houses for people with mental disabilities; and supported accommodation for people with intellectual disabilities. The common thread is not a single clinical intervention, but sustained residential support under government management.

That management model is central to who carries out the activity. The record identifies it as a government-operated service and does not list any business scale as open to registration. This is therefore a category framed around public provision of residential supervision, counselling and care, rather than an activity presented as open across stated enterprise scales. Its practical character is institutional and continuing: the work encompasses the living environment as well as the support offered within it.

Nationally, the PMA status is **TERTUTUP**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **0%**. In plain terms, foreign ownership is not available for this activity. Bali reaches the same operational conclusion: it is marked **TERTUTUP** and blocked for PMA registration. The Bali record adds an important distinction without changing that outcome. It identifies the activity as Medium-High or High risk, so it is not caught by the province-wide permanent PMA moratorium that applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. That does not create an opening for foreign registration: Bali’s recorded status remains closed, with verification required for the specific address.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s recorded status remains closed, even though this activity is not caught by the province-wide low-risk moratorium.
